stories.headline: Stripe in talks to buy AI model marketplace OpenRouter for about $10 billion

key_facts.fact: The Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday, July 23, that Stripe is in talks to acquire OpenRouter, and that a transaction could be announced soon, though talks could still fall apart.
key_facts.excerpt: Stripe is in talks to acquire OpenRouter, a buzzy startup that helps developers choose between artificial-intelligence models, according to people familiar with the matter. A transaction could be announced soon, though the talks could still fall apart or another suitor could emerge.

key_facts.fact: Some people familiar with the matter said OpenRouter could fetch about $10 billion in a sale; PitchBook data puts its most recent valuation at $1.3 billion in May.
key_facts.excerpt: The startup was valued at $1.3 billion in May, according to PitchBook, meaning a sale near $10 billion would represent a steep markup in a matter of months.

key_facts.fact: OpenRouter, founded in 2023, sells software that lets customers reach models from OpenAI and Anthropic plus open-weight alternatives, listing hundreds of large language models developers can compare and switch between.
key_facts.excerpt: Founded in 2023, OpenRouter sells software that allows customers to easily access AI models built by OpenAI and Anthropic, as well as "open weight" alternatives that are free for anyone to download and run. The company lists hundreds of large language models on its platform.

key_facts.fact: OpenRouter's backers include Menlo Ventures and CapitalG, Alphabet's growth fund; several other large technology companies had also been weighing deals for the startup.
key_facts.excerpt: Several other large technology companies had also been weighing deals for OpenRouter. ... Its backers include Menlo Ventures and CapitalG, the growth fund of Google parent Alphabet.

key_facts.fact: Stripe, whose valuation hit $159 billion earlier this year, already has a partnership with OpenRouter, which uses Stripe to accept payments from its customers.
key_facts.excerpt: Stripe - whose valuation hit $159bn earlier this year - is mainly a payments processor... OpenRouter and Stripe also already have a partnership together, where OpenRouter uses Stripe to accept payments from its customers.

key_facts.fact: The approach lands while Stripe pursues a separate bid for PayPal that would value the payments company at about $53 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: It also lands while Stripe pursues a far larger target: a bid for PayPal that would value the payments giant at about $53 billion.

stories.headline: Black Forest Labs launches FLUX 3, its first video model, and a robotics version tested at Audi

key_facts.fact: Black Forest Labs released FLUX 3 in early access on July 23, a multimodal model trained jointly on images, video and audio that generates clips of up to 20 seconds with native synchronized audio.
key_facts.excerpt: Flux 3 can now generate videos with native audio for the first time, with clips up to 20 seconds long. It supports text-to-video, image-to-video, video-to-video, keyframe-based transitions, multilingual dialogue, and agent-driven links between clips.

key_facts.fact: In the company's own preliminary preference tests on 10-second 720p clips, FLUX 3 was preferred over Luma Ray 3.2 in 93% of comparisons, Runway Gen-4.5 in 77%, Grok Imagine Video in 69%, Kling v3 Pro in 60%, and Seedance 2.0 and Gemini Omni Flash in 52% each.
key_facts.excerpt: Across early evaluations, FLUX 3 was preferred over Grok Imagine Video in up to 69% of comparisons, Kling v3 Pro in 60%, Happy Horse v1 in 59%, Happy Horse 1.1 in 57%, Seedance 2.0 and Gemini Omni Flash in 52%. FLUX 3 was preferred over Runway Gen-4.5 in 77% of comparisons and over Luma Ray 3.2 in 93% of comparisons.

key_facts.fact: Black Forest Labs and Swiss startup mimic robotics also introduced FLUX-mimic, a video-action model built on the FLUX 3 backbone that is being tested and deployed with manufacturers including Audi.
key_facts.excerpt: Black Forest Labs and mimic robotics today also introduced FLUX-mimic, a video-action model built on FLUX 3. FLUX-mimic is currently undergoing testing and deployment with leading manufacturing companies, like Audi.

key_facts.fact: Depending on task difficulty, FLUX-mimic can be fine-tuned for a specific manipulation task with as little as 30 minutes of robot data, where prior approaches required 30 or more hours.
key_facts.excerpt: BFL and Mimic Robotics say that depending on task difficulty, the model can be finetuned for a specific manipulation task with as little as 30 minutes of robot data, where prior approaches have required 30 or more hours.

key_facts.fact: Audi is testing the model on door-seal installation, a soft-material assembly task conventional automation has struggled with; BFL says the full system reacts in about 101 milliseconds.
key_facts.excerpt: Car maker Audi is already testing it on tasks like fitting flexible door seals, work that conventional automation has struggled to handle. ... BFL says the full system reacts in about 101 milliseconds, in the neighborhood of human visual reflexes.

key_facts.fact: FLUX 3 Video and FLUX 3 Action are in early access now, FLUX 3 Image rolls out in the coming weeks, and an open-weight FLUX 3 Dev version of the multimodal backbone is planned for later in 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Video and audio generation and editing through APIs and private weight access ("FLUX 3 Video"); Action prediction through selected research and commercial partners, beginning with mimic robotics ("FLUX-mimic and FLUX 3 Action"); Image synthesis and editing through APIs and private weight access ("FLUX 3 Image"); Open-weight access to a multimodal backbone ("FLUX 3 Dev").

key_facts.fact: FLUX 3 is already being tested by Canva, Burda, Magnific (formerly Freepik), Krea and Picsart, and the FLUX family powers generative features in Adobe Photoshop and Picsart.
key_facts.excerpt: FLUX 3 is already being tested by Canva, Burda, Magnific (formerly Freepik), Krea, and Picsart. ... powering generative features inside leading creative, developer, and consumer platforms like Adobe Photoshop, Picsart, Nous Research's Hermes Agent, and more.

stories.headline: Microsoft swaps OpenAI's image models out of PowerPoint and Bing for its own MAI models

key_facts.fact: Microsoft is replacing OpenAI's image-generating models with its own technology in products including PowerPoint and Bing; AI chief Mustafa Suleyman said MAI models are about 85% cheaper to run in PowerPoint.
key_facts.excerpt: "It's faster, it's cheaper, it's higher quality, it drives better retention," Microsoft AI chief Mustafa Suleyman said in an interview. ... Suleyman said the company's Microsoft AI (MAI) models are about 85% cheaper to run in PowerPoint, for example.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft AI put two new in-house models into public preview on July 23: MAI-Image-2.5-Pro, its highest-fidelity image model, and MAI-Voice-2-Flash, a speech model that is 2x faster and 32% cheaper than MAI-Voice-2.
key_facts.excerpt: MAI-Image-2.5-Pro is now in public preview. ... Pro is our highest-fidelity image model to date, priced at $5 per 1M text input tokens, $8 per 1M image input tokens, and $106 per 1M image output tokens. MAI-Voice-2-Flash is now in public preview. ... Flash is 2x faster than MAI-Voice-2 and 32% cheaper, priced at $15 per 1M characters.

key_facts.fact: Bing Image Creator is now 100% in-house, with MAI-Image-2.5 as the default model powering it end to end.
key_facts.excerpt: Bing Image Creator is now 100% in-house. With MAI-Image-2.5's new precise image editing capabilities, it is now the default model powering Bing Image Creator end-to-end.

key_facts.fact: In PowerPoint, Microsoft says MAI-Image-2.5 reduces GPU costs by up to 84% compared with GPT-Image-2, OpenAI's image model; in OneDrive it reports a 26% rise in save rates and roughly 25% lower P95 latency.
key_facts.excerpt: In PowerPoint, Microsoft says MAI-Image-2.5 reduces GPU costs by up to 84% compared with GPT-Image-2, OpenAI's image model. In OneDrive, where MAI-Image-2.5 is now the default for key image-editing scenarios, the company reports a 26% increase in save rates, roughly 25% lower P95 latency, and 2.5 times greater efficiency.

key_facts.fact: Suleyman said MAI models are now used in more than half of all Microsoft products and are being tested in all of them; Microsoft says its MAI models in Excel are on par with OpenAI's GPT-5.6 for common tasks while being more cost-efficient.
key_facts.excerpt: MAI models are now being used in more than half of all Microsoft products and tested in all of them, Suleyman said. ... Microsoft said that MAI models in Excel are on-par with OpenAI's GPT-5.6 for common tasks while being more cost-efficient.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft still gets free access to OpenAI models under its partnership, but pays for the computing infrastructure to run them, so cheaper in-house models translate into direct savings.
key_facts.excerpt: For now, the company gets free access to OpenAI models owing to its longstanding partnership. Still, Microsoft must provide the expensive computing infrastructure to run these models, meaning it can realize significant savings by using more efficient ones.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft says the MAI models are running in production across Bing, PowerPoint, OneDrive, Dynamics 365, Excel, GitHub Copilot and Azure.
key_facts.excerpt: it arrives with an unusual level of specificity about where those models now run: Bing, PowerPoint, OneDrive, Dynamics 365, Excel, GitHub Copilot, and Azure.

stories.headline: OpenAI opens ChatGPT Health to all US adults, wiring in medical records and Apple Health

key_facts.fact: OpenAI said on July 23 it is making Health in ChatGPT available to all logged-in US users aged 18 and over, on web and iOS, across the Free, Go, Plus and Pro plans.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI said today it is making ChatGPT Health, a feature that helps users with health-related queries, available to all U.S.-based users over 18 across all plans. ... Health in ChatGPT is rolling out to logged-in U.S. users with free, Go, Plus, and Pro plans on the web and iOS this week.

key_facts.fact: Users can connect Apple Health data and medical records from hospital systems running Epic and Oracle Health, as well as One Medical and Function Health.
key_facts.excerpt: Users can connect Apple Health data and supported medical records, including records available through hospital systems connected to Epic and Oracle Health electronic health record systems, along with One Medical and Function Health, OpenAI executives said.

key_facts.fact: Health information can now be used across normal conversations rather than only inside the dedicated hub; during testing OpenAI found 70% of health-related queries happened outside that hub.
key_facts.excerpt: The company said during the testing it observed that 70% of health-related queries took place outside the dedicated hub. Through this new feature, users can use their health information to get information on food or allergies in the general chat.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI's vice president of health product Ashley Alexander said in a briefing that the company's models 'are now capable of reasoning at levels that are better than clinician level.'
key_facts.excerpt: During a briefing, Ashley Alexander, OpenAI's vice president of health product, says the company's models "are now capable of reasoning at levels that are better than clinician level."

key_facts.fact: OpenAI says connected medical records, Apple Health information and conversations that use them are not used to train its foundation models or to target ads, and get additional encryption.
key_facts.excerpt: Tweet by @OpenAI: Health in ChatGPT is starting to roll out to U.S. users. You can securely connect Apple Health and supported medical records... Connected medical records and Apple Health information are not used to train foundation models or target ads.

key_facts.fact: The rollout came a day after a Florida-based pastor sued OpenAI, alleging ChatGPT gave a near-fatal suggestion not to consult a doctor; OpenAI's terms still say its services are not intended for diagnosis or treatment.
key_facts.excerpt: The announcement comes a day after a Florida-based pastor sued the company for giving a near-fatal suggestion not to consult a doctor. ... the company maintains in its terms that its services are "not intended for use in the diagnosis or treatment of any health condition."

stories.headline: OpenAI puts ChatGPT Voice in the desktop app to control the computer and direct multiple agents

key_facts.fact: OpenAI announced on July 23 that ChatGPT Voice is now in the desktop app, letting users control their computer and direct multiple agents running in ChatGPT Work or Codex using only their voice.
key_facts.excerpt: Tweet by @OpenAI: ChatGPT Voice is now in the desktop app. Control your computer and direct multiple agents running in ChatGPT Work or Codex, using just your voice.

key_facts.fact: The feature is powered by a model OpenAI calls GPT-Live, which it says can speak, listen and coordinate work in the app at the same time.
key_facts.excerpt: Tweet by @OpenAI: It's powered by GPT-Live, so it can speak, listen, and coordinate work in the app at the same time.

key_facts.fact: It began rolling out globally the same day on macOS and Windows to Plus, Pro, Business, Edu and Enterprise plans.
key_facts.excerpt: Tweet by @OpenAI: Rolling out globally today on macOS and Windows to Plus, Pro, Business, Edu, and Enterprise plans.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI said ChatGPT Voice can also be used in Codex from the iOS app with paired remote access, with Android support coming soon.
key_facts.excerpt: Tweet by @OpenAI: You can also use ChatGPT Voice in Codex from the iOS app with paired remote access. Android support is coming soon.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI president Greg Brockman promoted the launch, writing 'voice makes you feel just how unnatural it is to type' and urging users to try ChatGPT voice in the desktop app.

stories.headline: Bret Taylor's Sierra buys Takeoff, a three-person agent startup near $10M in revenue

key_facts.fact: Sierra announced on July 23 that it is acquiring Takeoff, a maker of long-horizon AI agents, for undisclosed terms; the two will build a new platform called Horizon.
key_facts.excerpt: Sierra announced it is acquiring Takeoff, a company that has grown from $0 in annual recurring revenue at the start of the year to nearly eight figures in revenue as of earlier this month. Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed. Together, the two companies are building a new platform called Horizon.

key_facts.fact: Takeoff went from $0 in ARR at the start of 2026 to nearly eight figures of revenue as of early July, and spent the last 14 months building a long-horizon agent runtime.
key_facts.excerpt: Since the beginning of this year, Takeoff has gone from $0 in ARR to nearly 8 figures of revenue as of earlier this month. ... We've spent the last 14 months building Takeoff into a long-horizon agent runtime that enables agents to operate like humans but scale like software.

key_facts.fact: Takeoff reached that near eight-figure run rate with a three-person team, closing several seven-figure contracts across five industries from lending to healthcare.
key_facts.excerpt: Takeoff was approaching a near 8-figure run rate with a 3 person team. ... Across five industries spanning lending to healthcare, Takeoff agents have beaten competing agents in head-to-head tests and consistently outperformed the processes, systems, and people in place before them.

key_facts.fact: Sierra co-founder Bret Taylor said the two companies made the same bet: that fully autonomous agents would perform human-level work at software scale and that the largest AI businesses would be built around outcomes, not inference.
key_facts.excerpt: it became clear we were making the same bet: that fully autonomous agents would perform human-level work at software scale and that the largest businesses in AI would be built around outcomes, not inference.

key_facts.fact: The deal follows Sierra's $950 million funding round in May 2026 at a valuation of more than $15 billion, and its partnership with SoftBank Corp.
key_facts.excerpt: The move follows Sierra's recent announcement of Horizon and its previously announced partnership with SoftBank Corp, as well as a $950 million funding round the company raised in May 2026 at a valuation of over $15 billion.

key_facts.fact: Takeoff's approach is to build end-to-end, industry-specific solutions and get paid directly based on the outcomes they produce rather than treating inference as a commodity.
key_facts.excerpt: Takeoff, founded 14 months ago, built an agent runtime designed to allow AI systems to perform long-horizon tasks, complex assignments that require reasoning, decision-making and interaction over extended periods.

stories.headline: Alphabet filing shows its private AI holdings, led by Anthropic, at $124.3 billion

key_facts.fact: Alphabet's quarterly report says the carrying value of its non-marketable equity securities accounted for under the measurement alternative was $124.3 billion as of June 30, 2026, of which $87.9 billion was remeasured at fair value during the quarter.
key_facts.excerpt: As of June 30, 2026, the carrying value of our non-marketable equity securities accounted for under the measurement alternative was $124.3 billion, of which $87.9 billion was remeasured at fair value during the three months ended June 30, 2026.

key_facts.fact: That is up from $64.1 billion at December 31, 2025, and the filing says the holdings 'primarily consist of our investment in a private company.'
key_facts.excerpt: Carrying value of non-marketable equity securities accounted for under the measurement alternative: 64,094 | 124,259 ... As of June 30, 2026, our investments in non-marketable securities accounted for under the measurement alternative primarily consist of our investment in a private company.

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg reported, citing a person familiar with the matter, that the figure is driven primarily by Alphabet's stake in Anthropic.
key_facts.excerpt: Filing: the value of Alphabet's investments in unidentified private companies was ~$124.3B as of June 30, a source says driven primarily by its Anthropic stake.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic's private valuation rose from $350 billion to $965 billion during the second quarter after a $65 billion funding round, while SpaceX went public in early June at a $1.77 trillion valuation.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX, in which Google owned a roughly 6% stake at the end of 2025, went public in early June at a valuation of $1.77 trillion... Anthropic, meanwhile, saw its private-market valuation jump from $350 billion to $965 billion in the same period.

key_facts.fact: Alphabet's Anthropic position began with a $300 million investment in April 2023 and has grown to $13.3 billion invested plus commitments of up to $30 billion more; Anthropic has committed to buying at least five gigawatts of Google Cloud computing capacity.
key_facts.excerpt: Alphabet's enormous paper windfall is the result of a prescient bet on Anthropic that began in April 2023, with an initial $300 million investment into Anthropic that has since grown to $13.3 billion, plus commitments of up to $30 billion more. As part of the arrangement, Anthropic has committed to purchasing at least five gigawatts of computing capacity from Google Cloud.

key_facts.fact: Most of the $99 billion in 'other income' Alphabet reported for the quarter came from its AI investments, primarily Anthropic and SpaceX.
key_facts.excerpt: Most of the $99 billion in "other income" is from Alphabet's AI investments, primarily Anthropic and SpaceX.
